content.text: {"label":"unknown_supply_issue","explanation":"General's handle time jumped sharply in the 10:30 interval: 744.9 s against 363 s forecast, more than double. Until then it was close to plan. Nothing on the demand side explains it. General volume is 10% under forecast today, and no call reason is meaningfully elevated (other_general is only 1.14x normal). There is no marketing campaign, and the 2 sick calls are within the usual 2.5 per day. The pattern looks like system slowness: calls take longer without more of them arriving. But the only incident logged is an overnight batch that is already resolved, and the spike covers a single interval, so the cause is not confirmed. Payments is unaffected, with AHT on or below forecast. The effect is a large loss of general capacity: roughly 58 Erlangs of work against 35 agents if the spike persists. Service level is still 91.3% for now but will fall quickly.","plan_name":"General AHT spike – protect capacity while cause is investigated","rationale":"The cause is uncertain and the spike may be short-lived, so the plan starts with free and cheap levers and adds a modest, time-boxed overtime offer. Delaying general breaks from 10:45 to 12:00 by 30 min keeps agents on phones through the likely peak. Cancelling non-mandatory general coaching until 13:00 returns capacity. The IVR callback offer on general, for callers facing waits over 120 s, smooths queue build-up. Deflecting 20% of balance_enquiry calls (about 23% of general calls) to chat cuts load for a few rupees per chat. Overtime for 10 general agents offered from 11:15 to 13:15 should bring about 4 acceptances, costing about Rs 2,880 and well within the Rs 15,000 budget. No agents are moved from payments: its 10:30 volume is back at forecast with 89.7% SL and about 34 Erlangs of work on 40 agents, so it has little margin to stay at or above 70%.
